clue.text: No clarity initially in spy lens

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows
in places the preceding pieces inside the word that comes next

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of clarity
a mole is a spy planted inside an organisation

explanation.surface: A spy complains that his optical gadget gives him no clarity at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spy' and 'lens' look like one picture of an agent's spyglass; spy is the wordplay, a mole being an agent planted inside an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A monocle is a single eyeglass, a lens worn in one eye.

clue.text: Game explorer of the thirteenth century

blocks.note: first meaning: a sport played on horseback with mallets
second meaning: Marco, the Venetian traveller to China

explanation.surface: A game invented by a medieval explorer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests one thing linked to the other; they are two separate meanings of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a mounted team sport, and Marco Polo travelled to Kublai Khan's court in the 1270s.

clue.text: Copper bottom cut from freezing dome

indicators.note: in a down entry the bottom is the last letter, so the final letter is removed

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
polar means icy cold

explanation.surface: A metal-clad dome on a bitterly cold building, its copper base sliced off.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer the bottom of a word is its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small rounded dome crowning a roof.

clue.text: Having secured contract finally, author in need of a drink

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
having secured means holding something firmly inside

blocks.note: Graham Greene, English novelist
last letter of contract
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer who has just signed a publishing deal wants a celebratory drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Graham Greene is a favourite crossword author; 'in need of' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is a beverage made from unfermented tea leaves.

clue.text: Composer not me, unfortunately: another composer

indicators.note: something that has gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters fall out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange
Giuseppe Verdi, Italian opera composer

explanation.surface: A composer laments that a rival, not he, got the commission.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer of early opera and madrigals.

clue.text: Art recreated within you for public performance

indicators.note: recreated means made over again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged
within places one piece inside the word that follows

blocks.note: thee is the old form of you
the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Art is staged afresh inside your space for a public show.
explanation.walkthrough: Thee is the archaic word for you, as in old prayers and poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre means drama staged before an audience, a public performance.

clue.text: Company working to split proportion of profit – that's hairy and tough!

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the thing, not a synonym

indicators.note: splitting something opens it up so other letters can sit in the gap

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a machine that is working is on
a cut is a share of the takings

explanation.surface: A tough, hairy boss's firm muscling in on someone's share of the takings.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description rather than a synonym: the fruit's fibrous husk and hard shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A coconut has a fibrous husk and a very hard shell, so it is literally hairy and tough.

clue.text: Old chip halved inside cheese roll

indicators.note: halved means cut down to only half of its letters
inside places the preceding pieces within the word that follows

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
taken as written, before halving
a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: An old chip broken in two and stuffed into a cheese sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese roll' reads as one sandwich, but cheese is wordplay and roll alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a soft, sweet, enriched bread bun, a kind of roll.

clue.text: Yellow bloom, as it happens, crimson

blocks.note: a lily is a flower
live broadcast is shown as it happens
crimson is a shade of red

explanation.surface: A flower described in colours, yellow and crimson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yellow' reads as a colour beside crimson, but it means cowardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellow in the slang sense of cowardly is exactly what lily-livered means.

clue.text: Crazy reason one's attached to the train

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the thing

blocks.note: loco is slang for mad
a motive is a reason for acting

explanation.surface: Someone fanatically devoted to trains, for some mad reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attached to the train' sounds like a fond enthusiast; it is the engine physically coupled to the carriages.
explanation.definitionFit: A locomotive is the engine coupled to the front of a train to pull it.

clue.text: Mouth, bit to the left

indicators.note: in an across entry, moving to the left means reading from right to left

blocks.note: a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: A horse's mouth with the bit pulled over to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: Trap is slang for mouth, as in 'shut your trap'.
explanation.definitionFit: Trap is informal slang for the mouth.

clue.text: Boy admitting defeat where terms are laid out

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the first word takes the other inside

blocks.note: a boy's name
a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: A young man concedes defeat at the point where the terms of surrender are set out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' suggests conditions of a treaty; they are words and their meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a list of specialist words with their meanings.

clue.text: Builder so set on man getting sacked

indicators.note: a sacked town is ransacked and thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A builder so determined to get a man fired.
explanation.definitionFit: A stonemason is a craftsman who builds with cut stone.

clue.text: Drunk near TV in pub

indicators.note: someone drunk staggers about, so the letters lurch into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A drinker slumped near the television in a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house where drink is served.

clue.text: Dogmatic rambling in a director

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about aimlessly, so the letters stray out of order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A film director who rambles on is also rigidly opinionated.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctrinaire describes someone who applies a theory rigidly, without regard to practicalities.

clue.text: Rhea, for example, bird on a headland

blocks.note: a tit is a small songbird
taken as written
a ness is a promontory, as in Dungeness

explanation.surface: A rhea, a large flightless bird, standing on a cliff top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhea' looks like the South American bird, which fits 'bird' nicely; here it is the Titan goddess, mother of Zeus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Rhea was one of the female Titans, so she is an example of a titaness.

clue.text: Sainted: devilish as an alternative

indicators.note: devilish suggests mischief, the letters being wickedly jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Saintly or devilish: take your pick.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface sets saint against devil; one is the letters, the other the instruction to shuffle them.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, that is, as an alternative.

clue.text: Entering days of September, start of season dry

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so one piece is placed within the other
the start of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: September has thirty days
first letter of season

explanation.surface: Weather notes: the autumn season begins dry in September.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside THIRTY, the number of days in September.
explanation.definitionFit: Thirsty means needing a drink, i.e. dry in the informal sense.

clue.text: Eat, tongue-in-cheek by the sound of it?

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the answer is heard as the phrase, not spelt like it

blocks.note: tongue-in-cheek means said jokingly

explanation.surface: A question whether eating was meant as a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tongue-in-cheek' also hints at food in the mouth, which suits eating.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food into the body, i.e. to eat it.

clue.text: Faculty certainly welcomed by rowing team

indicators.note: being welcomed by someone means being taken in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen
yes is an affirmation like certainly

explanation.surface: A university faculty member warmly received by the college boat crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' suggests a university department; here it is a power of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the faculty of seeing, one of the bodily senses.

clue.text: Lead first of children into English class

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the following word
into places that letter inside the word for class

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a sort is a kind or class
first letter of children

explanation.surface: A teacher leads the first of the children into the English classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: E comes first, then C inside SORT.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort is to accompany and guide someone, to lead them.

clue.text: Feature of Sicily has some cachet, naturally

indicators.note: has some says the following words contain a portion of themselves to be lifted out

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Sicily's great landmark naturally carries a certain prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano dominating eastern Sicily, its best-known natural feature.

clue.text: Old playwright: is he afraid of Santa?

blocks.note: Noel is Christmas, as in Father Christmas, Père Noël
a coward is someone who is afraid

explanation.surface: A whimsical question whether a famous dramatist is frightened of Father Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: The playwright's name reads as 'a coward of Noel', i.e. scared of Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward was an English playwright of the twentieth century, author of Private Lives.

clue.text: Signal breaker, for example

blocks.note: first meaning: gesture with the hand
second meaning: a breaker is one type of crashing sea swell

explanation.surface: A signal-breaker sounds like a codebreaker at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A breaker is a large sea swell that breaks into foam on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to gesture with the hand and a ridge of water on the sea, of which a breaker is one kind.

clue.text: Go low to puncture vessel

indicators.note: to puncture is to pierce, so one piece pushes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: a vase is a vessel for flowers
to low is to moo like a cow

explanation.surface: Instructions to drop down and pierce a ship's hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like 'below'; it is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for leave quickly, as in the command to go away.

clue.text: Possible reason for dropping it in juice

indicators.note: in places the preceding word inside the following one

blocks.note: gravy is the juice from cooked meat
taken as written

explanation.surface: Spilling something into the gravy, perhaps through clumsiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping' suggests clumsily letting go; the reason anything falls is the pull of the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravity is the force that makes objects fall, so it is why things drop.
